title: Solar Power Boiler as a Solution for Delivery Costs
excerpt: What are feed-in costs, and can I minimize them with a solar water heater or Water Battery? We explain it in this blog.
contentHtml:
What is the solar water heater? We call it the Water Battery, and it comes down to the same thing!
The netting scheme disappears and delivery costs are charged. How can you take maximum advantage of your solar panels and minimize delivery costs?
In this blog we explain how the solar power boiler, also called Water Battery, can limit the return costs by increasing your own use of solar energy.

Solar panels and Delivery costs

Solar panels are super popular with households in the Netherlands. And that is not surprising: sustainable energy and lower energy bills! However, the netting scheme is disappearing and since this year all energy suppliers have introduced feed-in costs. These are costs that energy suppliers charge when households with solar panels return unused electricity to the grid. Since the generation mainly takes place when many people are not at home, on average only 31% of the generation is used directly by the household. Fortunately, the solar power boiler or Water Battery offers a promising solution to minimize these feed-in costs

What exactly are Delivery Costs?

Delivery costs are fees that energy companies charge for solar power that households return to the electricity grid. The reason behind these costs is that the infrastructure must be maintained to manage the power in a safe and efficient manner. In the past, returned current was often settled at the same price as the decreased current (salding). With the rise of feed-in costs and the abolition of the netting scheme, households are faced with higher costs for their returned electricity.

Households with relatively few solar panels are likely to see little difference in their energy bill. Households with a lot of work, without an electric car or home battery, can certainly pay more. The exact return costs vary per energy company. But for everyone: you can use your solar energy better than you can deliver it back!

The Solar Power Boiler, from Water Battery, as a solution

A solar power boiler, we call it the Water Battery, offers a smart way to prevent the return costs and to make optimal use of the generated solar power. This solution uses the idle electricity from solar panels to heat water, which can then be used for household purposes such as showering and in the kitchen. Instead of returning unused energy to the grid, the energy is used directly in the house. What’s great about this: it also ensures that households also save gas, because most households still heat their water with the central heating combination! That is why the solar water heater or Water Battery provides significant savings on energy costs.

Note: a solar water heater is not the same as a solar water heater! A solar water heater consists of collectors (no solar panels) on the roof, which collect solar heat with a chemical liquid. This liquid is pumped around, and heat is released into tap water in a storage vessel (boiler). A solar power boiler uses the existing solar panels, and simply consists of an electric boiler and the Nymo from Solyx Energy. The investment in a solar water heater is therefore much lower than a solar water heater. In addition, installation is also a lot easier.
Because the terms solar water heater and solar water heater are quite similar, we use the term Water Battery.

Benefits of the Water Accu

  • Lower Energy Costs: Heating tap water to idle solar energy instead of gas saves most households significantly.

  • Increased Self-consumption: The Water Battery increases the self-consumption of generated energy, which is attractive given the return costs and the reduction of the netting scheme.

  • Environmentally friendly: The use of renewable energy sources such as solar energy to heat water reduces dependence on fossil fuels and contributes to lower CO2 emissions.

  • Independence from Energy Prices: By being less dependent on external energy sources, price fluctuations, the netting scheme and feed-in costs, households can better control their energy costs.

Conclusion: the Water Battery (or solar water heater) as a solution for feed-in costs

Delivery costs are a new challenge for households with solar panels, but making better use of their own generation is a good plan anyway. The Water Battery, also known as the solar water heater, can effectively minimize these costs. By using the generated solar energy directly to heat water, households can not only save on their energy bills, but also contribute to more sustainable energy consumption. Investing in a Water Battery is therefore a smart move for those who want to get the most out of their solar energy and at the same time be prepared for changes in the energy market.
